extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers and aspiring authors working on dialogue (novels, short stories, scripts)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for crafting effective, engaging spoken exchanges in fiction that reveal character, advance plot, and control pace. Focuses on stylistic, structural, and revision-oriented rules of thumb for authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue Is Easy Like Sunday Morning
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers flow through dialogue quickly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dialogue to move readers rapidly through scenes — its readability differs from prose and can be a tool to speed pacing and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Easy Isn't The Same As Uncomplicated
rubrics_metrics.description: Although dialogue reads easily, it can and should convey complex narrative elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't mistake smooth readability for shallowness; use dialogue to carry subtext, character, and thematic complexity even while keeping it accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sweet Minimalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Rely on 'said' and 'asked'; avoid excessive adverbs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer simple dialogue tags (said/asked) over flashy verbs and modifiers; overusing adverbs or tag-verb variety often distracts instead of clarifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uh, You Do Know The Rules, Right?
rubrics_metrics.description: Master proper formatting and punctuation for dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure dialogue is correctly punctuated and formatted (quotations, paragraph breaks, tag placement) so the reader isn't pulled out of the scene by technical errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use It To Set Pace
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue accelerates reading speed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ dialogue to quicken momentum in scenes; balance dialogue and prose to control pacing deliberately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shape Determines Speed
rubrics_metrics.description: Short, sharp dialogue is fast; long exchanges slow tempo.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary line length and exchange structure to modulate tempo: staccato lines for urgency, extended speeches for slowdown and reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expository Dialogue Is A Pair Of Cement Shoes
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid info-dump dialogue that awkwardly feeds background or exposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep exposition out of contrived conversations; find organic ways to reveal necessary information without halting natural speech or believability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing Through Telling
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue conveys info while preserving 'show, don't tell.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let characters reveal facts and feelings through spoken interactions and subtext rather than through explicit narrator summary or direct telling.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Wart On The End Of The Nose
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters shouldn't bluntly state their exact feelings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid lines where a character flatly declares emotions; instead, show feelings through choice of words, tone, and action in dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Words Beneath The Words
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtext matters more than literal meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write dialogue that carries an underlayer of implication — the unspoken wants, fears, and agendas beneath the surface speech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay No Attention To The Dead Man Behind The Curtain
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue conceals as much as it reveals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use withholding and evasions deliberately; not everything needs to be stated — silence and omission can deepen mystery and characterization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where Tension, Suspense And Mystery Have A Big Crazy Gang-Bang
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue generates suspense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage conversational ambiguity, interrupted thoughts, and withheld information in dialogue to create and sustain tension and mystery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quid Pro Quo, Clarice
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice and personality emerge through how characters speak.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let differences in diction, rhythm, and priorities in speech reveal character; give each speaker distinct aims and strategies in conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let The Character Sign Their Own Work
rubrics_metrics.description: Speech patterns reveal distinct identity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft idiosyncratic phrasing, dialect, or recurring verbal ticks so readers can identify speakers and understand personality from dialogue alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue Is A Theme Park
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters can orbit thematic elements through conversation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use dialogue to explore and echo your story's themes without being didactic — let characters touch on thematic concerns naturally as they speak.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue Is Action
rubrics_metrics.description: Speaking constitutes action; characters move while talking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat dialogue as part of the scene's activity: combine speech with physical beats and consequences, so talk propels events and choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Real World Is Not Your Friend
rubrics_metrics.description: Real speech ('um', 'like') doesn't translate well to fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filter everyday filler and false starts; aim for authentic-feeling speech that remains readable and purposeful in service of story and character.

rubrics_metrics.name: For The Record, You're Not David Mamet
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't mimic overlapping dialogue without skill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid attempting complex, rapid-fire overlapping dialogue patterns unless you can execute them clearly — they can confuse readers if mishandled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Again: Not A Ping-Pong Match
rubrics_metrics.description: Characters interrupt and pursue agendas; avoid mechanical back-and-forth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make conversations driven by desires and interruptions rather than sterile alternating lines; give each turn a purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversation Is Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective dialogue arises from conflicting goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame dialogue as negotiation, power-play, or contest — even casual talk should reveal competing wants to create interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authenticity Trumps Reality
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue should feel genuine, not literally accurate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture the emotional truth and voice of speech rather than slavishly reproducing verbatim real-world dialogue, which can be messy and dull.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sometimes, You Just Gotta Babble That Shit Out
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow rambling first; refine in revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Free-write initial dialogue to find voice and beats, then edit ruthlessly to shape clarity, pace, and subtext in later drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nothing Wrong With Banter
rubrics_metrics.description: Casual interaction reveals personality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use light, playful exchanges and repartee to show relationships and character without derailing plot — banter can be revealing and entertaining.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Greatest Crime Against Humanity Is Writing Boring Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain sharp, engaging exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make every line do work — if dialogue bores, cut or intensify it; keep stakes (emotional, informational, or dramatic) present to hold attention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double-Duty Dialogueing
rubrics_metrics.description: Dialogue develops character, theme, plot, tension simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for multi-layered lines that serve more than one purpose so dialogue remains efficient and richly functional within the story.
